description:
FILED s470bm (Opus, 2026-09-05) by the Part B item B4 census (#1172).  All
PRE-EXISTING.  MEASURED, not fixed — B4's brief is to find and gate them.

WHAT A LEAK IS.  ir-spec §11b: a PCL-emitted file may contain only the
runtime's exported names (§10a), the 100-name whitelisted CL kernel, literals,
and the program's own identifiers.  A bare CL FUNCTION in operator position is
none of those: a JS or C backend cannot run the file without also implementing
that host function.  Nothing else in the tree sees it — the gate runs the CL on
SBCL, where `(concatenate 'string …)` works perfectly, and corpus-diff compares
two emissions of the same compiler.

THE MEASUREMENT (`tools/ir-host-leak.pl`, s470bm):
  perl-tests (111 files, 175,317 tokens)     38 distinct leaked symbols
  lib/**.pm  (22 files, module mode)         only `use integer`'s, in
                                             lib/Math/BigInt/Calc.pm
  perl's own t/ (592 files, 522,620 tokens)  the same set plus #1178 and #1179

THE FAMILIES, each with its trigger (every one probed down to a minimal
fixture, which is what Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t runs):

1. `use integer` — ONE pragma emits nine bare CL operators.
   `Pl/ExprToCL.pm:1595-1610` returns ['truncate'|'rem'|'+'|'-'|'*'] and
   ['p-to-s64', ['logand'|'logior'|'logxor', ['pcl::%pcl-to-integer', …]]]
   directly.  Fixture: `use integer; my $x = length("abc") % -10; my $b = 5 & 3`
   -> op:* op:rem op:truncate op:logand op:logior op:logxor op:lognot
      op:pcl::%pcl-to-integer   (the last one is #1177's family too)

2. The SIGNATURE-DEFAULT arity test — `(> (length @_) 0)`.  86 occurrences in
   perl-tests/signatures.t, 87 in perl's own.  Fixture:
   `use feature 'signatures'; sub f ($a = 222) {…}` -> op:>

3. `\x{…}` escapes and `tr///` ranges — `(concatenate 'string (string
   (code-char 55296)) …)`.  Fixture: `my $s = "\x{d800}\x{ffff}"`
   -> op:code-char op:concatenate op:string quoted:string

4. The `__DATA__` handle's registration — `(make-string-input-stream "…")`.
   MEASURED and worth writing down because the obvious guess is wrong:
   `open my $fh, '<', \$scalar` does NOT reach it.  44 of perl's own t/ files
   carry it.  Fixture: a program with a `__DATA__` section -> op:make-string-input-stream

5. A `\(LIST)` refgen over more than one element — CL's `loop` macro with its
   `for` / `across` / `do` keywords.  `\(1 .. 2)` alone does not reach it.
   Fixture: `my(@fuu) = \(1..2,3)` -> op:loop

6. Residue with no single trigger yet: `op:-` and `op:+` on negative literals
   (`(- #x80001218)`, perl-tests/arith.t:598), `op:1+`/`op:1-` in array-length
   arithmetic (`(1+ _prev)`), `op:eq`, `op:format` (yadayada's message),
   `op:intern` (perl-tests/lc.t:78).

THE FIX DIRECTION is the same for all of them: route the emission through a
`p-*` op (existing or new), so the vocabulary stays closed.  None is urgent —
they are all CORRECT on the CL target — but each one is a file a foreign
backend must refuse.

THE GATE that exists now: `Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t` (924 ms) runs one fixture
per family and asserts the EXACT leaked set, in both directions — a new symbol
is a new leak, a missing one means the family closed and the row, this task
and ir-spec §11b's table must be updated together.  The population census
(`tools/ir-host-leak.pl`, ~40 s over 111 files) is the WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN item
for a `cl/**` or `Pl/**` change; it is NOT in the gate (8.4 s for six real
corpus files, more than a gate file may spend).

BAR when taken: the family's fixture leaks nothing; corpus-diff explains every
emission diff; the gate; the full sweep if the change is in `cl/**`.

=== PARTLY DONE (s470bo): families 2, 3, 4 and 5 CLOSED; 1 and 6 stay open ===

Four of the six families are one named op each, with the Â§10a `Contract:` tail
and a row in the regenerated inventory:

  family 2  the signature-default arity test   `p-arg-supplied-p`   (macro)
  family 3  `\x{â¦}` escapes and tr/// ranges   `p-literal-string`
  family 4  the `__DATA__` handle              `p-install-data-handle`
  family 5  `\(LIST)`'s spread                 `p-vector-append`    (macro)

Two are MACROS on purpose: the emission then costs exactly what the inline
form cost, so the IR gains a name without the generated code gaining a call.

WHAT EACH TAKES OUT beyond its own head:
* family 2 removes `>` (86 occurrences in signatures.t alone) AND collapses two
  hand-written copies of the availability test in `Pl/Parser.pm` into one.
* family 3 removes FOUR names plus a quoted host TYPE designator â
  `(concatenate 'string (string (code-char 55296)) â¦)` becomes
  `(p-literal-string 55296 65535)`, a bad code point being an INTEGER argument
  and a piece of text a string argument.  The `'string` was one of #1176's
  three meanings of a quoted symbol, so THAT finding shrinks to two.
* family 4 removes `make-string-input-stream` AND the quoted handle name
  `'DATA`: the emitter wrote the setf, the gethash, the special variable and
  the constructor out; it now names the operation.
* family 5 removes `loop` â the one CL macro whose body is a language of its
  own, and so the worst thing to leave in an IR for a backend to parse.

MEASURED: leak census over the 111 perl-tests files **41 distinct at the start
of the session, 38 after #1177, 31 after this**.  `corpus-diff.pl` = 10 of 111
files differ, and the explanation is exact: those are the ONLY ten whose
emission contains one of the four ops (`p-install-data-handle` in anonsub,
magic, method, readline, reset, sprintf, state; 86 Ã `p-arg-supplied-p` in
signatures; 31 Ã `p-literal-string` in tr; `p-vector-append` in ref).  The
1015-file wide A/B: 156 diffs, 127 carrying exactly one new op (119 of them
`p-install-data-handle` â most perl test files have an `__END__`) and the other
29 already explained by #1178/#1179.  Inventory: 0 UNCLASSIFIED.  Four VALUE
rows in `Pl/t/census-bugs-01.t`, because the point of a rename is that nothing
observable changes.

`Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t` keeps a row per closed family with an EMPTY expected
set, so a re-opened family fails a gate row instead of going unnoticed, and
each row's `why` says when and why it closed.

STALE GUARD PAID IN THE SAME SESSION (the s416 rule): `Pl/t/wide-codepoint-01.t`
rows 5 and 6 spelled `(concatenate 'string â¦)` out and failed the moment
family 3 landed â repaired with the same claims in the new spelling.

=== NOT DONE, and why ===

FAMILY 1 (`use integer`, nine bare CL operators: `truncate` `rem` `+` `-` `*`
`logand` `logior` `logxor` `lognot`).  This needs a `p-*-int` runtime op per
operator, which is the emission half of the already-filed **#1000** ("`use
integer` bypasses every operator's dispatch") â the same nine emission sites,
and the place where `use integer` stops skipping overload dispatch.  Doing it
here as a pure rename would have to be redone by #1000, so it is #1000's.
The ONE thing this session took out of family 1 is `pcl::%pcl-to-integer`,
which #1177 exported.

FAMILY 6 (`-` and `+` on negative literals, `1+`/`1-` in array-length
arithmetic, `eq` on `*wantarray*`, `format` in yadayada's message, `intern` in
lc's symbol lookup).  No single trigger; the census names the sites and each
is a different one-line emission.  Sized: `1+`/`1-` is `['p-+', X, 1]` at two
`Pl/ExprToCL.pm` sites; `eq` is a `(p-in-list-ctx)` macro over three sites;
`format`/`intern`/the negative literals are one site each.  Cheap but five
unrelated edits â a filler, not this task.


=== REGRESSION AND FIX, family 4, same session (s470bo) ===

The first shape of `p-install-data-handle` took only the TEXT and interned its
own `'DATA` â which is `pcl::DATA` for every caller.  `*p-filehandles*` keys on
the SYMBOL and `DATA` is PER-PACKAGE in perl, so the program and every module
it loads shared one key; perl's own `Exporter.pm` has an `__END__` POD section,
so anything that pulls Exporter REPLACED the program's DATA section.

MEASURED: perl-tests/sprintf.t 532 passing -> 0 (it planned ONE test, described
`> < >< >< > < `, having read one record of Exporter's POD instead of its
566-row `__END__` table); readline.t 23 -> 21.  Fable's full sweep caught it.

FIXED: the handle is an ARGUMENT â `(p-install-data-handle 'DATA "â¦")`, the
symbol interned by the emitter in the file's own package, exactly where it was
before.  `make-string-input-stream` still stays out of the IR, which was
family 4's actual leak; the quoted handle NAME comes back and that is #1176's
meaning (c), the handle model, declined by this session as a new mechanism.
After: sprintf.t 532/25 (planned 559), readline.t 23/5 â the pre-regression
numbers.

WHY THE PROBES MISSED IT, for whoever touches this family next: a standalone
file's two-line `__DATA__` works, `scalar(<DATA>)` works, a ten-line section
with blank and `#` lines works â a program that loads no module with an
`__END__` has no collision.  `<DATA>` even RESOLVES (`%p-resolve-fh` falls back
by NAME to the `:pcl` symbol), the separator is `"\n"` and the stream is at
position 0 at loop entry, and 566 records are readable right after the DATA
form.  The discriminating measurement is ONE probe: print every
`*p-filehandles*` key whose name is "data" together with its PACKAGE.
    before  ((DATA "MAIN") (pcl::DATA "PCL"))
    after   ((pcl::DATA "PCL"))          <- one key, two writers
A guard row for this family must put the COLLISION IN THE FIXTURE (`use
Exporter`), or it tests nothing.  The two rows added do, and both read in LIST
context â the spelling sprintf.t does not use.
subject: HOST LEAKS: 38 distinct bare CL symbols reach the emitted IR through v1 seams (use integer, signature defaults, \x{} escapes, __DATA__, refgen loop) - measured, gated, not fixed
